# 13 Resolve and validate interaction and styling declarations

## Outcome

`buildClassModel` resolves interaction and styling declarations against real classes and enforces
this board's security boundary: an `href` must use an allowed scheme, and a style value must not
smuggle in a fetchable or executable construct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An interaction or style declaration targeting an unknown class produces an error diagnostic
  and is dropped; the rest of the model resolves.
- [ ] `http:`, `https:` and `mailto:` URLs resolve. A `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:` or
  scheme-relative (`//evil.example`) URL is **dropped** with an error diagnostic naming the
  rejected scheme — the class still renders, just without a link.
- [ ] A relative URL (`./docs/shape.html`) resolves — the allowlist rejects dangerous schemes, it
  does not require absolute URLs.
- [ ] A style value containing `url(` or `expression(` is dropped with an error diagnostic; the
  other declarations in the same `style` statement still apply.
- [ ] A style property name that is not a plain CSS identifier is dropped with an error diagnostic
  (no `;`-smuggling a second declaration through one value).
- [ ] `cssClass` applying an undefined `classDef` name produces an error diagnostic.
- [ ] `classDef` declarations merge onto a class in application order, with a later `style`
  statement on the same class taking precedence.

Also close this id-collision bug, found in round 3's review and living in this file:

- [ ] **Namespace and note ids can collide with relationship ids.** A relationship's id is
  `${from}-${to}`, and namespaces/notes are numbered `namespace-${n}` / `note-${n}` — so a class
  literally named `namespace` pointing at a class named `1` produces a relationship whose id is
  `namespace-1`, identical to the first namespace's. Verified with a real document: no diagnostic,
  and both `timeline:` addressing and `data-siren-id` become ambiguous. Class ids are `\w+`, which
  cannot contain `:`, so a separator the relationship convention can never produce (`namespace:1`,
  `note:1`) resolves it outright. Whatever you choose, an author has to type these ids in a
  `timeline:` block, so keep them readable — and say in the report what an author now writes.

## Test seam

`buildClassModel(document: ClassDocument): ClassModelResult` — unit level, hand-built fixtures,
extending the existing test file. Every rejection case above gets its own test: this is the
board's security boundary, and a silently-passing allowlist is worse than none.
